newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French insurer UAP shows first-half profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French insurer UAP shows first-half profit.

text.p: France's largest insurer UAP, coming back from a large 1995 full-year loss, reported on Tuesday a 6.7 percent rise in first-half profit and said it was on track for a return to "lasting profitability".
Net attributable profit rose to 860 million francs ($166.5 million) from 806 million francs a year earlier on turnover rose 6.6 percent to 86.35 billion francs from 81.02 billion.
The company's shares jumped nearly four percent, climbing to 111.0 francs, as investors welcomed UAP's confident profits outlook.

UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann called the results "healthy" and said in a statement they had been achieved despite a sharp reduction in capital gains. "They are solid and constitute a measure of our future progress," he said.
In 1995, UAP, Europe's second largest insurance group, posted a full-year loss of 2.07 billion francs, the first in its history, as it struggled to clean up its books.

The loss included an exceptional second-half charge of 4.5 billion francs that included big provisions against doubtful property loans in wake of the collapse of French real estate prices and as well as against asset depreciations.
Following the loss, Friedmann announced a major drive to cut costs, slash debt, restructure its international operations and dispose of assets in order to restore profitability.
"These (results) are the first effects," he said. Friedman said that doubtful property loans were now limited to just 1.1 billion francs and that risk provisioning was now 69 percent.
He forecast that UAP, privatised two years ago, would produce a profit in the second half similar to the first half.
"In current market conditions, the group should produce a profit in the second half similar to that of the first, thus confrming our return to lasting profitablity," Friedmann said.
"For the first time in several years, the improvement in our pre-tax, pre-exceptional result is finally showing through in ouir net consolidated profit," he said.
The half-year profits were powered by the contribution from insurance operations which jumped to 2.03 billion francs from 1.77 billion francs.

Profits from banking activities soared to 245 million francs from 61 francs, helped by a strong performance by French bank BNP in which it holds a 14 percent stake. Its troubled Banque Worms unit cut its losses to 26 million francs from a loss of 63 million.
But the loss from holding companies deepened to 776 million francs from a loss of 422 million, reflecting exceptional charges of 535 million. ($ = 5.165 French Francs)
